questions.title: Capillary hydrostatic pressure drives bulk flow
questions.subject: cvs
questions.module_subject: SCU-FBS102 > Physiology > Cardiovascular Physiology > Capillary Exchange
questions.question: The hydrostatic pressure gradient established across the capillary wall predominantly drives which of the following physical processes?

options.C: Bulk flow of fluid through capillary pores
options.D: Slow active transport of large water-soluble proteins

explanations.A: Incorrect. Water-soluble drug movement across the capillary wall, where it occurs through pores, is itself governed by the same bulk-flow (and diffusion) principles, but the hydrostatic gradient specifically drives bulk flow, not a distinct 'rapid diffusion' process for drugs.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Lipid-soluble gases cross the capillary wall by simple diffusion through the endothelial cell membranes themselves, a process driven by their own concentration (partial pressure) gradient, not by capillary hydrostatic pressure.
explanations.C: Correct. The hydrostatic pressure gradient between the capillary lumen and the interstitium is the Starling force that drives bulk flow — the mass movement of fluid and its small dissolved solutes together through the capillary wall's pores — producing filtration where hydrostatic pressure dominates. This distinguishes bulk flow from simple diffusion, which moves individual solute molecules down their own concentration gradient rather than fluid in mass.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Large plasma proteins do not normally cross an intact capillary wall in appreciable amounts by any active transport process; their near-impermeability is what generates the opposing oncotic pressure in the first place.

questions.learning_objective: State that bulk flow across the capillary wall is driven predominantly by the hydrostatic pressure gradient, and distinguish it from diffusion of individual solutes.
